keyword: how fast will artemis 2 enter the atmosphere
claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule will re-enter Earth's atmosphere at approximately 24,000 to 25,000 mph (38,300 to 40,200 km/h) on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entry marks the fastest crewed reentry in history.
The extreme speed allows the Artemis II Orion capsule to return from the Moon.
The re-entry creates temperatures around 5,000°F on the heat shield.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hits the upper atmosphere at roughly 34,965 feet per second.
34,965 feet per second is about 23,800–25,000 mph.
The heat shield faces temperatures of ~5,000°F (2,700°C).
The craft's trajectory is specially managed to manage the heat.
The capsule will slow down using parachutes to a splashdown speed of 17 mph.
The splashdown will be in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II re-entry is faster than the previous crewed record holder, Apollo 10.
The high-speed return marks the final phase of the mission.
The high-speed return requires intense thermal protection, as noted in updates from NASA.
